trails.title: Chilika, through a poet’s eyes
trails.alt: A passenger boat and birds on Chilika Lake.
trails.text: Read a place before you reach it. The Chilika story connects the lagoon with Gopabandhu Das’s poem about seeing it from a train, and points towards Radhanath Ray’s Chilika.
trails.prompt: Give yourself a quiet moment to look. What would make you ask the journey to pause?

trails.title: Balasore, beyond the map
trails.alt: A garlanded commemorative bust of Fakir Mohan Senapati.
trails.text: Fakir Mohan Senapati was born near Balasore. Begin with his life, then follow Six Acres and a Third into questions about land, power and everyday people.
trails.prompt: Carry a question into the book. Whose story do you hear first—and who has yet to speak?

trails.title: Mayurbhanj, in living words
trails.alt: The name Ol Chiki written in Ol Chiki script.
trails.text: Follow the connection between Mayurbhanj, Raghunath Murmu and Ol Chiki. Santali belongs to living conversations, classrooms and literature as well as a script’s history.
trails.prompt: Begin by listening. Ask a willing speaker which word, story or book they would choose to introduce their language.
